literal: The battle-axe of desire will break the door called self-control, which is fastened by the bolt of shyness.
translation: The battle-axe of desire will break open the door of my self-control, which is secured by the bolt of modesty.
modern: நாணம் என்னும் தாழ்ப்பாள் போடப்பட்ட நிறை (மனக்கட்டுப்பாடு) என்னும் கதவை, காமம் என்னும் கோடரி உடைத்துவிடும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the speaker describes how overwhelming love-passion overpowers their reserve. The poet employs a vivid metaphor of a house: the mind's self-control (niraiv) is a protective door, and modesty (nāṇ) is the strong bolt securing it. However, the intense desire (kāmam) acts as a sharp battle-axe (kaṇicci) that easily shatters this bolted door, exposing the hidden feelings. This illustrates the helplessness of a lover when passion exceeds the limits of modesty.
